comparator.name: Psychobiologie
comparator.academicYear: Current UvA 2026–2027 published bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official curriculum lists complete 60-EC first- and second-year programmes. In year 3 it permits 30–42 EC of electives and an 18-, 24- or 30-EC Bachelor Project. This coherent 180-EC pathway selects the 30-EC Bachelor Project and 30 EC of genuine elective space, without inventing particular elective courses or a formal route. The programme is explicitly research-oriented and combines biology with psychology, with biological emphasis.
components: Philosophy of Science and Statistical Reasoning
A coherent 30 EC elective package is selected within the published 30–42 EC choice range.
The published Bachelor Project may be 18, 24 or 30 EC; the 30-EC version is selected to complete a coherent 180-EC pathway with 30 EC of electives.

core: Psychobiology integrating biological and psychological explanations of brain, body and behaviour
Cellular, molecular and physiological neuroscience, including neurotransmitters and brain–body regulation
Cognition, perception, attention, consciousness, memory, emotion, motivation and decision-making
Experimental design, statistics, programming, data analysis, laboratory work and scientific reporting
Development, evolution and biological foundations of behaviour across the life course
Neurobiology of mental health, addiction, depression and atypical behaviour
adjacent: Cognitive neuroscience and computational analysis of perception, language and brain data
Molecular neuroscience, psychopharmacology and mechanisms of neurological or mental disorder
Evolutionary psychobiology and the evolution of behaviour and cognition
questions: How do biological processes in the brain and body generate cognition, emotion and behaviour?
How can experiments, brain measurement and data analysis reveal mechanisms of perception and behaviour?
How do molecular and neural mechanisms contribute to mental health, addiction and disease?

alternatives.label: Brain, biology & behaviour
alternatives.concept: Combines cellular and molecular biology, neurobiology, physiology, cognition, perception, psychology, mental health and experimental research to explain behaviour from biological processes to higher-order human functions.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme spans biological foundations, brain systems, cognition, behaviour and health rather than presenting itself as either biology or psychology alone.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, data and philosophical foundations precede physiology, pharmacology, disease, perception, advanced cognition, psychology and research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Cognitive neuroscience, perception & data
alternatives.concept: Emphasises cognitive neuroscience and computational analysis of perception, higher-order functions, language and development, combining neurobiology and experimental psychology with programming, statistics, machine learning and brain-inspired models.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained and visible weight to cognition, perception, language and quantitative/computational methods for interpreting complex behavioural data.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces much of the molecular biology, physiology, pharmacology and disease material with programming, machine learning, neural networks, computer vision, mathematics and cognitive modelling. It differs by well over 30 EC and centres the analysis of cognition and data.
progression: Brain, neurobiology, mathematics and programming foundations precede experimental methods, machine learning, perception, neural networks, language, advanced cognition and independent research. All prerequisites and offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Molecular neuroscience, health & disease
alternatives.concept: Emphasises the molecular, cellular and physiological basis of brain function and disorder through biochemistry, molecular cell biology, genetics, pharmacology, anatomy, neurobiology, perception, disease mechanisms, laboratory work and biomedical data.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is anchored in molecular and biomedical mechanisms while retaining neurobiology, perception, experimental methods and quantitative analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: This route differs from the broad and cognitive-data programmes by replacing much of their psychology, philosophy and language content with biochemistry, molecular cell biology, genetics, anatomy, pharmacology, laboratory science, immunology and disease mechanisms. It passes the 30-EC floor against both earlier programmes.
progression: Life science, brain and behaviour, programming, evolution and data foundations precede physiology, biochemistry, molecular biology, anatomy, neurobiology, pharmacology, genetics, laboratory work and disease. All prerequisites and offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The first programme is the closest broad psychobiology response. Cognitive-neuroscience/data and molecular-neuroscience/health directions are explicit official study directions, form coherent curricula and pass all feasibility and pairwise distinctness gates. Evolutionary psychobiology remains evidenced but is not attempted after the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: UvA Psychobiology provides a tightly sequenced laboratory curriculum in genetics, cell biology, neuroanatomy, neurophysiology, EEG and molecular experiments, culminating in a large scientific internship. UCR can combine substantial biology, neuroscience, psychology and data study, but it does not reproduce the same dedicated laboratory sequence or 30-EC placement.
